result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s2.json`. Riley got three items correct, two partial and one wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Feedback |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only writes the tool request, and the program runs the tool. This improves on the first attempt. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | Riley chose to let it run longer. The same failure repeats, so more steps add nothing. The agent needs a step limit, which Riley got right the first time. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | The answer of 4 is right, but the stated reason, that the model runs the tools itself, is wrong. The program runs them, and each tool result triggers a new model call. |
| q5 | correct | Riley covered both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide its next step. |
| q6 | partial | Riley said the model picks by name only. It chooses from the full description: name, purpose and parameters. |

**Summary:** Riley has the core of the loop. Two things need work. The model never runs a tool, and an agent needs a stopping condition. The model also needs full tool descriptions, not just names.

I also added `learning-records/0003-model-requests-program-runs.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` is still ungraded.

**Next step:** Riley should write a description for `check_calendar` with its purpose and parameters. Then trace one request, marking which steps the model does and which the program does.

Do you want me to grade `s1` as well, so the two attempts can be compared?
